title: GRE tunnels to Zscaler: where each question is answered

prose.text: GRE is the unencrypted site tunnel from a router to ZIA Public Service Edges. Its behavior is held in the ZIA traffic forwarding subjects; this subject routes the questions.

steps.label: Is GRE the right method?
steps.text: Router support, a static egress IP and the comparison with IPSec, PAC files and Client Connector: [[zia.traffic-forwarding.methods]] and [[zia.traffic-forwarding.gre:static-ip-required]]. The vendor's recommended combination of methods is [[zia.traffic-forwarding.methods:recommended-combination]].

steps.label: Where is it built from?
steps.text: An internal router behind the firewall (preferred), the border router with NAT disabled, or explicit proxy mode to the Global Public Service Edges where there is no default route: [[zia.traffic-forwarding.gre:internal-router]], [[zia.traffic-forwarding.gre:border-router]], [[zia.traffic-forwarding.gre:explicit-via-global-edges]].

steps.label: How much does a tunnel carry?
steps.text: The 1 Gbps and 250 Mbps limits, the NAT reason and scaling with more source IPs: [[zia.traffic-forwarding.gre:bandwidth-limit]], [[zia.traffic-forwarding.gre:scale-out]].

steps.label: What MTU and MSS?
steps.text: The 1,476-byte MTU and 1,436-byte MSS for a 1,500-byte WAN: [[zia.traffic-forwarding.gre:mtu-mss]].

steps.label: How is failure detected and failed over?
steps.text: Keepalives, Layer 7 health checks to the vpntest URL, and the fast and conservative failover profiles: [[zia.traffic-forwarding.gre-failover]].

steps.label: How is the tunnel provisioned?
steps.text: Static IP, VIP selection, the excluded premium data centers and the API: [[zia.traffic-forwarding.gre:provisioning]], [[zia.traffic-forwarding.gre:vip-selection]], [[zia.traffic-forwarding.gre:api-surface]].

prose.label: Client Connector behind GRE.
prose.text: Zscaler says not to route Z-Tunnel 2.0 through GRE: [[zcc.z-tunnel.deployment:gre-guidance]]. Why several egress IPs break Z-Tunnel 2.0 setup is [[zia.traffic-forwarding.mixed-deployments:gre-ztunnel2-egress]]; the Z-Tunnel side is [[shared.z-tunnel]].

prose.label: Users and addresses.
prose.text: How GRE inner addresses map to sublocations is [[zia.locations.ip-scoping]], and user identity on tunnel traffic comes from Surrogate IP: [[zia.authentication.surrogate-ip]]. How the firewall sees tunnel traffic is [[zia.firewall.traffic-path]].
